messages.author: 6b412994c5d0ef5c
messages.subject: GBS_denovo_mapping
parts:
Hi,

I am using R/qtl to map 25K SNP on RIL population (90 individuals). I am a beginner on R/qtl so I trait to follow the tutorial:

 GBS_SLB <- read.cross("csvr",file="GBS_to_rqtl.csv", estimate.map=FALSE)
GBS_SLB <- convert2riself(GBS_SLB)
summary(GBS_SLB)
    RI strains via selfing

    No. individuals:    90

    No. phenotypes:     1
    Percent phenotyped: 100

    No. chromosomes:    1
        Autosomes:      1

    Total markers:      25867
    No. markers:        25867
    Percent genotyped:  72.9
    Genotypes (%):      AA:51.6  BB:48.4
Warning messages:
1: In summary.cross(GBS_SLB) :
  Duplicate markers [Lsat_1_v3_g_0_1701_260001]
2: In summary.cross(GBS_SLB) :
  Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length; there may be a problem with the genetic map.
  (Perhaps it is in basepairs?)
however, I got:
> GBS_SLB <- est.rf(GBS_SLB)
Error: cannot allocate vector of size 2.5 Gb
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lod[lower.tri(lod)] <- t(lod)[lower.tri(lod)] :
  Reached total allocation of 32764Mb: see help(memory.size)
2: In lod[lower.tri(lod)] <- t(lod)[lower.tri(lod)] :
  Reached total allocation of 32764Mb: see help(memory.size)
3: In lod[lower.tri(lod)] <- t(lod)[lower.tri(lod)] :
  Reached total allocation of 32764Mb: see help(memory.size)
4: In lod[lower.tri(lod)] <- t(lod)[lower.tri(lod)] :
  Reached total allocation of 32764Mb: see help(memory.size)
>

however, I guess I have good memory:
> memory.size(max = FALSE)
[1] 30728.3
> memory.limit(size = NA)
[1] 32764

so, someone has some advice? maybe someone wants to share your experience with GBS data?

thanks,
Carlos

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] GBS_denovo_mapping
parts:
It's trying to allocate 2.5 Gb RAM, since est.rf will be attempting to estimate recombination fractions for all pairs of markers, and with 25,867 markers, there are 335 million pairs of markers.

You'll probably need to find another strategy, for example by working with subsets of the markers rather than the whole set.

karl
